title: fix: preserve surrogate pairs in shared and command truncation
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14562

Part of #14562 (shared string helpers and command-output paths; remaining paths listed below).

No breaking changes or grapheme-cluster guarantee; existing malformed input is not repaired.

The helper is exported from both shared entry points so core can reuse the node export while browser consumers retain the same shared string API.

title: feat(core): flag-gated computer-use section in the cloud session prompt
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A. This is part of the computer-use rollout for cloud sessions ("closing the loop"). Related: #15393 (artifact attach/render), core-platform #3577 (artifact endpoints), core-platform #3581 (sandbox learns its session ID).

### Description

This lets cloud-session agents check their own UI changes. Behind a new `cloud-computer-use` feature flag, the cloud session's system prompt gets a section that tells the agent how to:

- start a virtual display (Xvfb) in the sandbox,
- launch the app in Chromium,
- drive it with xdotool,
- take screenshots with ImageMagick,
- look at the screenshots with `read_files`,
- publish the frames that prove the change with `publish-artifacts --files <list.json> --attach`, so they appear in the user's chat.

This is the "main agent drives it directly" v1 we agreed on. Moving the work into a computer-use subagent and adding a `present` tool for captioned slideshows come later.

**Where it hooks in.** All clients create cloud tasks through the hub daemon's `CloudSessionController`. It builds the system prompt in `buildCloudSessionSystemPrompt` and sends it with `session.create`. Note that on the sandbox hub this prompt *replaces* the normal Cline prompt (`resolveBootstrapSystemPrompt` returns `config.systemPrompt` verbatim). So the new section is written to stand on its own instead of assuming the base prompt's tool guidance.

**Gating.** The section is added only when both of these hold:

1. **The model can see images.** It must be in the bundled `cline` catalog with the `images` capability. Models missing from the catalog are treated as text-only. This is deliberately stricter than `modelSupportsImageInput({})`, which assumes support when capabilities are unknown, so the section never reaches a model whose `read_files` would reject screenshots. The check runs first and is cheap, so non-vision models never hit the flag service.
2. **The flag is on.** This is `isClineAccountFeatureEnabled(FeatureFlag.CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE)`, the same account-scoped PostHog check Composio uses inside the hub daemon, where the client's in-memory flag service isn't available. It's cached for 60s and fails closed. For local development, `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1` in the environment the hub daemon inherits turns it on without PostHog.

The controller takes the gate as an injected `isComputerUseEnabled` option. That keeps the controller free of flag and env lookups and makes it easy to test. If the gate throws, the section is left out.

The section is added to both the new-task prompt and the local-to-cloud handoff prompt. It only affects new tasks: existing tasks keep the prompt they were created with.

**Prompt content.** It's adapted from the computer-use spec, with these changes:

- `chromium` instead of `google-chrome`, because the base image is Debian (`node:24-slim`), and window search by `--class chromium`.
- `--no-sandbox` added to the Chromium flags. Chromium's own sandbox doesn't work as a non-root user in this container.
- A tools check first (`command -v Xvfb xdotool import chromium`), with "skip, don't install" if anything is missing. The sandbox runs as `node` without sudo, and the tools arrive via the base image.
- The evidence-file folder (`/tmp/cu-shots/evidence/*.json`) is replaced with `publish-artifacts --attach`, which already exists on cloud-platform's `feat/session-artifacts` branch. The agent describes each published screenshot in its answer, since loose images have no captions yet.

### Test Procedure

- New controller tests:
  - The section is added when the flag is on and the model takes images.
  - It's left out when the flag is off.
  - It's left out when the model isn't in the catalog.
  - It's left out when the gate throws.
- `vitest run src/cloud/controller.test.ts`: 112 passed. `src/hub/server/cloud-session-service.test.ts`: 56 passed.
- `bun run typecheck` in core (dev + smoke) and `tsc` in shared are clean.
- I checked that the new `@cline/llms` import in `cloud/` doesn't reach the desktop webview: its `@cline/core/cloud` imports are type-only.

**Not yet tested end to end.** That needs pieces that haven't merged or deployed:

- core-platform #3581, so the sandbox gets `CLINE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`.
- cloud-platform `feat/session-artifacts`, which ships the `publish-artifacts` command, after #15393 merges and the SDK is released.
- The computer-use tools in the base image (Marlon).

Until those land, a flagged agent will find the tools missing and skip verification, as the prompt tells it to.

To try it once they land: run desktop with `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1`, start a cloud task on a vision model in a repo with a web UI, and ask for a visible change. Published screenshots should appear in the chat.

### Type of Change

-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Additional Notes

- The `cloud-computer-use` flag still needs to be created in PostHog. Until then everyone evaluates to off, except dev builds using the env override.
- The first flagged task per minute waits on one PostHog poll before `session.create`. The cache and fail-closed behavior bound this.
- Follow-ups: a `present` tool with title, captions and pass/fail (replacing loose images); a computer-use subagent to keep screenshots out of the main context; artifact rendering outside desktop.

body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** no GitHub issue; Linear DAT-111. This is a smaller alternative to #15043 that covers just the privacy settings link.

The diff is 224 added lines across 16 files, compared with 1,381 across 46 in #15043. The other parts of #15043 (the desktop sign-out race fix, `client=` attribution, and environment-aware links across the desktop app) can follow as separate PRs if they're wanted.

### Description

`GET /users/me` now returns `dataPrivacyPath` (for example `/dashboard/account?tab=privacy`), the Cline web app page where users manage Restrict Data Use and Cline Bench preferences. Each client shows a **Privacy settings** link only when the field is present, so older or self-hosted backends show nothing new.

- **`@cline/shared`:** `resolveClineAppUrl(path, appBaseUrl)`, next to `getClineEnvironmentConfig`. It resolves a path against the web app and returns `undefined` if either input is missing or the result would leave the app's origin (another host, protocol-relative, `javascript:`, plain `http`). The path comes from the server, so this keeps a bad value from becoming a link to somewhere else.
- **`@cline/core`:** `ClineAccountUser.dataPrivacyPath?: string`.
- **CLI:** the account snapshot builds `privacySettingsUrl` on the environment's `appBaseUrl`, and `/account` adds a **Privacy settings** action that opens it in the browser and leaves the dialog open.
- **VS Code and JetBrains:** `data_privacy_path` is added to the `UserInfo` proto and passed through `AuthService.getInfo()`. The Account view adds a **Privacy settings** button under Dashboard / Log out, using the same `appBaseUrl` as the Dashboard button. `ClineAuthContext` now replaces the user when any field changes, not only `uid`. Token refreshes re-fetch `/users/me` for the same user, so without this the new field would never reach the webview.
- **Desktop:** the Account view adds a shield **Privacy settings** button next to **Open dashboard**.

Deliberately not in this PR:
- No `client=` attribution parameter, since the dashboard doesn't read it yet.
- Existing dashboard links aren't migrated or hidden. Desktop links stay as they are, including those hardcoded to production, and the new desktop link uses `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl` like `welcome-chat.tsx`. Making every desktop account link follow the environment is a separate change.
- No handling for a provider `baseUrl` override when picking the web app.

### Screenshots

Not captured. The new controls only render for a signed-in account whose `/users/me` includes `dataPrivacyPath`. The controls match the ones in the #15043 screenshots.

title: fix(llms): give adaptive-thinking Claude requests the full output budget
body:
## Problem

Adaptive thinking (Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5) counts inside `max_tokens`. When no `maxTokens` is set, the gateway sends `max(32000, 0.3 × model.maxOutputTokens)` — **38,400** for these models. At `--thinking high` the models often think 20–70k tokens on one step, so the call is cut off mid-thought:

- the response has no answer text (finish reason: length), and the thinking is billed and discarded
- the agent then retries with the "output-token limit reached" nudge

In a DeepSWE benchmark campaign (Oct 20, OpenRouter, `--thinking high`), this showed up as ~6-minute calls with 0 output followed by the nudge.

## Fix

For adaptive-thinking requests (`isAdaptiveThinkingRequest`: Claude adaptive-era model id + reasoning enabled), the synthesized default uses the model's **full** advertised output budget (128k) instead of 30% of it.

- still clamped by the context window
- an explicit `maxTokens` still wins
- non-adaptive and non-Claude models are unchanged

## Testing

- New tests in `gateway.test.ts` (128k default, context clamp, explicit override) and `model-facts.test.ts`
- Wire capture: Opus/Sonnet 5.5 now send `max_tokens: 128000`; other models unchanged
- Reran 4 tasks × Opus/Sonnet × 3 on Prime with a 3.0.73 build containing this patch: **0 output-limit truncations** (previously frequent). Calls with 46–77k thinking tokens now complete instead of being cut off.

## Notes for reviewers

- This removes truncation; it does **not** make runs faster. At high effort calls that used to be cut off at ~6 min now finish (some take up to ~12 min). The slowness comes from `high` effort itself and is a separate default question.
- OpenRouter may reserve credit against `max_tokens`; a 128k request could hit "insufficient credits" for low-balance keys. Worth a sanity check.

body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15377

### Description

Commit search hands the typed query to a shell command, so the shell eats the quotes before `git log` sees them.

`apps/vscode/src/utils/git.ts` interpolated the query into a command string:

```ts
const { stdout } = await execAsync(
	`git log -n 10 --format="..." --date=short ` + `--grep="${query}" --regexp-ignore-case`,
	{ cwd },
)
```

With `"quoted"` as the query, `git` receives `--grep=quoted`, so it also returns commits that only contain the unquoted word. The same pattern was used for the hash fallback (`--author-date-order ${query}`) and for `getCommitInfo()`, where the revision comes from a mention (`@<hash>`) and was also spliced into the command string.

The file already solves this exact problem for file names, and says so:

```ts
// Pass the filename as a separate argv entry (no shell) so names containing

```

title: fix(llms): back off between in-stream provider retries
body:
## Cause

The AI SDK's `streamRetries` re-dials the moment a provider error part arrives, with no wait between attempts. A provider that is overloaded is still overloaded a few milliseconds later, so all four attempts fail the same way and the user sees the provider's message ("Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.") with a manual Retry button. In telemetry for 4.1.25 (Oct 20–23), 54% of the overload failures that reached users came through this path, and when users retried by hand 2–10 s later, 81% of those retries succeeded.

Two smaller problems on the same path:

- Capacity errors from OpenAI-compatible backends arrive as in-band error parts with no HTTP status. The AI SDK recognises only a few exact messages, so it types these as non-retryable, and our classifier had neither their provider codes nor a message fallback for them.
- The silent retry attempts left no telemetry, so no retry policy could be measured.

## Changes

- `stream-retry-backoff.ts`: `onError` now waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (cap 8 s) before the AI SDK's next in-stream attempt; the SDK awaits `onError` before re-dialing. No wait when no stream retry follows (request-start `RetryError`, transport failures, tool-choice violations) or when the failure reproduces on every attempt (credential, context window). Vendors can tune or disable it through `ProviderFactoryResult.streamRetryBackoff`.
- The wait is announced through `emitStatusNotice` ("provider error — retrying in 2s (attempt 2/3)"), which renders as an info row in VS Code and JetBrains and as a status line in the CLI. `GatewayStreamRequest` carries the callback from the agent runtime.
- `error-classification.ts`: provider capacity codes (`server_is_overloaded`, `service_unavailable`, `service_unavailable_error`, `overloaded`, `overloaded_error`, `model_overloaded`) and an `overloaded` message fallback count as retryable when no status is present.
- Telemetry: an `sdk.stream_retry` event per wait; the terminal `sdk.error` carries `streamRetryAttempts` and `streamRetryWaitMs`.
- `sleep` moved out of the empty-response middleware into its own module, shared with the backoff.

Fixes https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13356 ([CLINE-3015](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3015/error-our-servers-are-currently-overloaded-please-try-again-later)); the same failure was reported in a JetBrains Marketplace review on 2026-08-19.
Refs https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13606 ([CLINE-3088](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3088/task-aborts-on-transient-api-errors-timeouts-provider-outages-instead)) and [ENG-2350](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/ENG-2350/decision-auto-retry-parity-was-dropped-entirely-restore-or-accept). Request-start failures that exhaust the SDK's own `maxRetries` backoff (the other 46% of overload failures) are out of scope here.

## Tests

```bash
cd sdk/packages/llms && bunx vitest run src/providers/stream-retry-backoff.test.ts src/providers/gateway.test.ts src/providers/error-classification.test.ts src/providers/ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts
```

`ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts` drives the real `ai` package over the OpenAI-compatible wire format: an overloaded error frame, then a successful stream. It asserts that the re-dial waits, that the notice is emitted once, and that the retry's text is what the caller receives.

## Release note

Transient provider errors during a response (such as "servers are currently overloaded") are now retried with a short backoff and shown as a retry notice, instead of failing the request after four immediate attempts.

body:
Part of [CLINE-3681](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3681/cline-html-file-can-be-opened-within-cline-app-and-messed-up-whole-ui) (https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/issues/1241). The JetBrains side, which stops such a click from replacing the panel, is https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243.

## Problem

When the model links a local file in a chat message, e.g. `[Open index.html](/Users/me/project/index.html)`, `MarkdownBlock` rendered a plain anchor and left the click to the host. VS Code's webview drops it (only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `vscode` links are opened), so nothing happened. The JetBrains webview navigated to the resolved URL and lost the panel.

The host cannot do better: by the time the click is a navigation, the href has been through react-markdown's URL sanitising, which blanks `file:` URLs and `C:\` paths as unknown schemes, and through URL resolution against the webview origin, which turns `\\server\share` into `https://server/share`. The webview is the only place where the href the model wrote is still known.

## Change

- `localFileLink(href)` classifies an href as a link to a local file: an absolute POSIX, Windows or UNC path, a `file:` URL, or a scheme-less path relative to the workspace. Web links, other schemes and anchors are left alone. The markdown parser percent-encodes the destination (`C:\x` arrives as `C:%5Cx`, a space as `%20`), so a path is decoded back to what was written; a `file:` URL is passed on as is.
- `MarkdownBlock` keeps those hrefs through `urlTransform` and renders them with a click handler that opens the file through `FileService.openFile` (absolute, `file:`) or `openFileRelativePath` (relative) instead of navigating. The anchor's tooltip names the path. Other links keep their default behaviour.
- `openFile` in `integrations/misc/open-file.ts` turns a `file:` URL into the platform's path with `fileURLToPath`, so drive letters and UNC hosts are interpreted where the file lives. A file that cannot be opened still shows "Could not open file!".

## Testing

- `webview-ui`: `localFileLink.spec.ts` (classification, decoding, `file:` passthrough) and `MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx`, which renders real markdown through the component and checks the href, that the click is prevented, and which RPC is called with what.
- `open-file.test.ts`: absolute path passed through, `file:` URL converted.
- VS Code dev host on macOS: a model reply with five links. Absolute path, relative path and `file:` URL each opened the file in an editor tab; a `C:\...` path reached core as written and showed "Could not open file!" (expected on macOS); the `https` link opened the browser. The panel kept its state.
- JetBrains sandbox (IU 2025.1.7, with https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243): the same five links; absolute, relative and `file:` open the file through the host bridge, the Windows path shows "Could not open file!", the `https` link goes to the external browser, the panel keeps its state.
- Not run: Windows. The Windows and UNC cases are covered by the unit tests; the path reaches core unchanged and Node resolves it there.

```bash
cd webview-ui && bunx vitest run src/utils/__tests__/localFileLink.spec.ts src/components/common/__tests__/MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx
bun test src/integrations/misc/open-file.test.ts
```

## Release note

Links to local files in Cline's chat open the file in the editor.

title: fix(core): treat a 404/402 from the current-plan endpoint as no plan
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** none filed; found during a post-release telemetry check of desktop 0.0.49 / core 0.2.0.

### Description

#### What telemetry showed

In the first hours after the Oct 26 release, desktop 0.0.49 logged a new error, `no plan history found for user`, from the `cline_account` sidecar command:

- **135 signed-in machines in 3 hours, ~9% of all 0.0.49 machines**, ~2 events each.
- **Zero on 0.0.48.**

It's the only new error type in the release with that kind of reach. It's not a crash, but it inflates desktop error counts and puts the Account view on an error path for free users.

#### Cause

`GET /api/v1/users/me/plan` answers:

- **404** with `{"success":false,"error":"no plan history found for user"}` for anyone who has never had a plan;
- **402** when the plan is unpaid.

Both mean "not subscribed". `ClineAccountService.fetchCurrentUserPlan` (core) didn't distinguish them from a real failure. `request()` throws on any non-2xx, so every caller got a rejected promise.

- **Desktop:** `fetchClinePassModels` in `account-view.tsx` is written to return `null` when there's no plan (`plan?.plan?.entitlements`). It never got the chance, because the invoke rejected first, and the sidecar captured the failure as an `sdk.error`. The call became more prominent in 0.0.49, which is why the error appeared with this release.
- **CLI:** onboarding (`tui/views/onboarding/controller.ts`) already worked around this by string-matching the error message: `message === "no plan found for user"` → unsubscribed. **The API now says `no plan history found for user`**, so that match no longer fires and unsubscribed users land in the ClinePass *error* state instead of *unsubscribed*. That's a second, silent bug with the same root cause.
- **VSCode** was never affected. Its own account service (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/account-service.ts`, `fetchClinePassSubscribedRPC`) maps 404 and 402 to "not subscribed" and has a test for exactly that.

#### Fix

`request()` gains an `absentOnStatus` option: listed statuses resolve `undefined` instead of throwing, checked before the body is parsed. `fetchCurrentUserPlan` passes `[402, 404]`.

The return type was already `Promise<UserCurrentPlan | undefined>`, so every caller already handles `undefined` as "no plan":

- desktop's `fetchClinePassModels` returns `null`;
- CLI onboarding's fulfilled branch sets `"unsubscribed"` when `value?.plan` is empty.

No caller changes are needed. Other failures (401, 5xx, network, timeout) still throw exactly as before.

Why fix it in core rather than in each caller:

- one place, matching VSCode's semantics;
- removes the reliance on the API's error wording that broke the CLI;
- every other `fetchCurrentUserPlan` consumer gets the right behaviour for free.

The CLI's string match is now dead code for this case. I left it alone to keep the diff to the root cause; it's harmless and can go in a follow-up.

### Test Procedure

- `sdk/packages/core`: `vitest run src/account`: 4 files, 26 tests pass. New cases:
  - 404 with the real `no plan history found for user` envelope resolves `undefined`;
  - 402 resolves `undefined`;
  - 401 still rejects with the existing message.
- `apps/cli`: `vitest run src/tui/cline-account.test.ts`: 9 tests pass.
- `biome check` is clean on both files, and `tsc` reports no errors in `src/account`.

**After release:** desktop `sdk.error` events with `no plan history found for user` should drop to zero on the next desktop build.

title: fix(cli): isolate shell environments for sessions sharing a Hub
body:
Shell tools in a reused local CLI Hub inherit the daemon’s environment, which can lose the current terminal’s variables and retain stale daemon-only values.

Capture an immutable client environment snapshot when the CLI discovers its local Hub, validate it at the boundary, and use it for that session’s built-in shell children and delegated work. An absent field keeps legacy inheritance; an explicitly empty field creates an empty environment. SDK callers can opt in explicitly. The snapshot is scoped to execution and is not persisted. Explicit Hub endpoints and desktop clients do not automatically capture the CLI environment.

Both the CLI and Hub need the patch. Older Hubs silently ignore the new field; the compatibility documentation explains this.

Validation: [combined Linux/Windows CI passed](https://github.com/djbclark/cline/actions/runs/40279171772). It built the SDK, CLI and platform binaries, passed compiled Hub health smoke and both typechecks, and passed 3,286 Linux core tests, 1,310 CLI tests, two real shutdown tests, and 5,455 Windows SDK tests. Existing platform skips remain. Earlier focused source-mode checks and a failing base-host negative control cover fresh client values, stale daemon-key removal, isolation and serialization privacy.

The combined validation tree is reviewed feature head 7a4835e4ac823b3d45984ca737efd6632bf67bad plus the separate test-only Bun-version cleanup in https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15348 and upstream release metadata. This PR’s source remains separate. The macOS ARM64 artifact’s source/build commits and binary hash were verified. title: fix: check the ClinePass plan by HTTP status in the CLI, and re-check it when the user returns from Subscribe
body:
### Related Issue

Follow-up to #15302 / #15333: the ClinePass plan check that landed there, rolled out to the CLI, with Greptile's findings on both PRs addressed.

### Description

**CLI.** Onboarding decided "unsubscribed" by comparing the plan endpoint's error text to `"no plan found for user"`, which the server stopped sending in July. Every non-subscriber has since landed on "Could not verify your ClinePass subscription" instead of the subscribe prompt.

The server signals "no current plan" by status, not payload: 404 when there is no plan or it has ended, 402 when it is unpaid. ClinePass inference is refused in both cases. `ClineAccountService.fetchCurrentUserPlan` now resolves `undefined` for those two statuses and throws a `ClineAccountRequestError` carrying the status for anything else. The statuses live in one exported set, `NO_CURRENT_PLAN_STATUSES`, whose doc comment names the server's current-user-plan handler as the thing to keep in step with. Both names are exported from the `@cline/core` root so SDK consumers can branch on them (Greptile, this PR).

The CLI already treated a payload without a plan as unsubscribed; it now gets that path for the 404/402 answers too, and its two string matches are gone. The VS Code extension's own check reads the shared set instead of its own copy.

**Extension (Greptile on #15333).** The plan refresh ran only when the Cloud pane mounted and skipped any answer under a minute old. The Subscribe link opens the browser while the pane stays mounted, so a user who subscribed and came back still saw the notice and the usage-billed default. The pane now refreshes when the user comes back to the webview; a return after a Subscribe click forces the check past the recent-answer window and past any check already in flight, whose answer may predate the purchase. `CloudService.refreshClinePassSubscription` takes a `BooleanRequest` for that.

VS Code reports a return from the browser as window `focus`, `visibilitychange`, or both. `useGitHubConnection` listened for the first and the plan refresh for the second, so each missed the other's case. A new `useWindowReturn` hook listens to both, drops the hide transition, and coalesces the pair one return produces; both call sites use it. Other browser round-trips (account sign-in, Add credits, the ClinePass card and promo, Connect GitHub from outside the Run Task panel) don't yet listen for a return at all; they can pick up the hook in a later sweep.

### Test Procedure

```
cd sdk/packages/core
bunx vitest run src/account/cline-account-service.test.ts
cd -
cd apps/cli
bunx vitest run src/tui/cline-account.test.ts src/tui/views/onboarding
```

title: fix(llms): keep Anthropic prompt cache advancing through tool loops
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15307 (also #15167)

### Description

With the direct Anthropic provider, prompt caching stopped advancing during tool-call loops. Cache reads stayed flat at the size of the first prompt and nothing new was written, so every tool step was billed at the full input rate.

Cause: `buildAnthropicProviderOptions` set the request-level option as `cache_control`. `@ai-sdk/anthropic` strips that key. Only `cacheControl` gets mapped to the top-level `cache_control` that turns on Anthropic's automatic caching, which moves the cache point forward on each turn. Without it, the only breakpoint was the explicit one on the last `user` message. Tool results are sent as `tool` messages, so during a loop that breakpoint stayed on the original prompt.

The Cline and OpenRouter paths were not affected, because the openai-compatible passthrough already sends a top-level `cache_control`.

The fix gives `createEphemeralCacheControl()` an optional key parameter that defaults to the `cache_control` wire field. The Anthropic request-level option now calls it with `"cacheControl"`. All other callers and the per-part markers are unchanged, since the AI SDK accepts both spellings on parts. This is a much smaller alternative to #15174 with the same result.

| Request | Before: cache read / write | After: cache read / write |
|---|---|---|
| Initial prompt | 0 / 3,359 | 0 / 3,361 |
| After 1 tool round | 3,359 / 0 | 3,361 / 3,187 |
| After 2 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 6,548 / 3,188 |
| After 3 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 9,736 / 3,188 |

### Additional Notes

Requests now carry two breakpoints: the explicit one on the last user text and the automatic one. That is within Anthropic's limit of 4. Vertex Claude uses the same `anthropic` options bucket, so it will send the top-level flag as well. I did not test Vertex live.

title: feat(cli): send a task to Cline Cloud with --cloud
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (follow-up to #15317, stacked on it)

### Description

Adds `cline --cloud "..."` for sending a task straight to Cline Cloud without opening the TUI. It starts a new cloud session for this folder's GitHub repo (or the one passed with `--repo`), sends the prompt, and exits as soon as the sandbox accepts it, printing a link to follow along. The task keeps running in the cloud after the CLI exits, like `--zen` does for the local Hub.

```sh
cline --cloud "Fix the flaky retry test and open a PR"
git diff | cline --cloud "Review this change"
cline --cloud --repo cline/cline --branch main "Summarize the open TODOs"
```

How it picks things (same rules as the TUI's Cloud mode):
- **Repository:** this folder's git `origin`, which must be a GitHub repo the Cline account can access. `--repo owner/name` (a GitHub URL also works) overrides it, so `--cloud` works from any folder. Clear errors when there's no GitHub repo to use, the `--repo` value isn't a repo, GitHub isn't connected, or the account can't access that repo (with the access link).
- **Branch:** `--branch name` if given, checked against GitHub so a typo fails clearly. Otherwise the current local branch if it exists on GitHub (only when the repo is this folder's origin), otherwise the repo's default branch.
- **Model:** the saved cloud pick from the TUI's `/model`, otherwise the local Cline/ClinePass model if the cloud offers it (so `-m` works too), otherwise ClinePass for ClinePass users, otherwise `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. This logic moved into a shared `resolveCloudModel()` that the TUI hook now uses as well.
- **Mode:** Act with tools auto-approved in the sandbox.

Details:
- Gated by `CLINE_CLOUD_SESSIONS=1` like the TUI; `--cloud`, `--repo` and `--branch` are hidden from `--help` unless it's set, and using `--cloud` without the variable explains how to opt in.
- `--repo` and `--branch` only work with `--cloud` and are rejected without it.
- Piped stdin is appended to the prompt, the same as other one-shot runs.
- `--json` prints one `cloud_dispatched` line with `sessionId`, `url`, `repository`, `branch` and `model`; failures (startup checks included) print the CLI's usual `error` line.
- Can't be combined with `--tui`, `--id`, `--worktree`, or `--zen`.
- Runs before the local agent runtime loads, so it stays fast. `isCloudSessionsEnabled` moved to a tiny module so `program.ts` doesn't pull in `@cline/core` at startup.
- Documented in the CLI README next to Zen mode. `run-cloud.test.ts` covers exiting on acceptance while the turn keeps running, branch paging, an unknown `--branch`, and a rejected send.

### Additional Notes

- `--cloud` only starts new sessions. Following, replying to, or pulling a cloud session from the shell are natural follow-ups.

title: fix(compaction): correct the context-size estimate in both directions
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14979

### Description

Auto-compaction fired far below the real context window when the char-based token estimate overshot the provider's actual input count.

The correction in `compaction.ts` computes `actual / estimate` from the provider's previous request count, but clamps it with `Math.max(1, ...)`. A factor can only tighten the budget (estimate under-counting), never loosen it. With prose-heavy transcripts the chars/3 estimate reads ~1.5x the real tokens, so the trigger tripped near 60% of the real window.

Changes:

- `compaction.ts`: clamp the correction ratio between a new `MIN_INPUT_OVERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (0.5) and the existing `MAX_INPUT_UNDERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (4). - `compaction-shared.ts`: added `MIN_INPUT_OVERESTIMATE_FACTOR` with a comment explaining the bound.

The floor mirrors the existing cap: a wildly inflated estimate cannot push compaction past the real window.

title: fix(hooks): run UserPromptSubmit hooks for prompts seeded into the runtime
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14963

### Description

UserPromptSubmit hooks never ran for the user's actual message in CLI and desktop sessions.

Two different paths deliver the prompt to `AgentRuntime`:

1. A directly driven runtime gets the prompt as `run(input)` and emits it as `message-added`.
2. Orchestrated sessions (what the CLI and desktop use) append the user message to the conversation, seed it into `initialMessages`, and call `run("")`. No `message-added` event fires for that prompt.

The file hook layer only dispatched `prompt_submit` from `message-added`, so path 2 never fired the hook. The VS Code hooks adapter already handles this by scanning the `beforeRun` snapshot; this change does the same at the core file-hook layer and in the CLI's in-process hook dispatcher.

Changes:

- `createHookConfigFileHooks` now installs `beforeRun` when prompt_submit hooks exist and scans the snapshot for the latest user message that is not marked `displayRole: "system"`, dispatching `prompt_submit` there. If a run-start hook cancels the run, the prompt hook is skipped, matching the extension.
- `onEvent` keeps handling `message-added` for directly driven runtimes. Dispatched message ids are tracked so a `continue()` run, whose snapshot still contains earlier prompts, does not re-fire them.
- The audit hook layer records the same prompt_submit dispatch so `hooks.jsonl` reflects what the file hooks actually ran.
- Runtime-generated user-role reminders (completion-tool reminder, completion policy reminders, max-tokens recovery nudge, unexpected-turn continuation) are now marked `displayRole: "system"` so the snapshot scan does not mistake them for user prompts.
- The CLI's in-process hook dispatcher in `apps/cli/src/utils/hooks.ts` gets the same snapshot scan and dedup.

title: cli: publish musl builds for Linux
body:
Refs #15271.

## What

Adds musl Linux to the CLI's build matrix and publishes two more platform packages:

- `@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl`
- `@cline/cli-linux-arm64-musl`

The glibc Linux packages additionally get `"libc": ["glibc"]`, and the musl ones
`"libc": ["musl"]`, so npm's libc-aware optional dependency resolution
(npm >= 10.4) installs the right binary on each host instead of pulling in a
glibc build that dies in the loader.

## Why it was more than one line

Bun compiles these targets from any host (`bun-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`), and
`@opentui/core` already ships `core-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`. Two things were
still missing:

1. **OpenTUI picks its native library at runtime** from `OPENTUI_LIBC`,
   defaulting to glibc. A musl binary therefore extracted and loaded the glibc
   `.so` and failed with `Error loading shared library ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`.
   The target's libc is now baked in with a `define`, which also lets Bun
   tree-shake the variant it will never load (156 MB -> 143 MB).
2. **The npm wrapper and `postinstall.mjs` hard-code**
   `@cline/cli-<os>-<arch>`. Both now append `-musl` when the running Node has
   no glibc runtime, using Node's diagnostic report.

## Testing

Built all eight targets with the patched script (`bun script/build.ts
--install-native-variants --skip-sdk-build`, ~2 minutes) and ran the
`@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl` binary on **OpenWrt 24.10.8 / x86_64 / musl**
(`libstdcpp6` installed, which is the only extra system dependency — Bun's
musl runtime links `libstdc++.so.6`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cline --version` | `3.0.73`, 0.8 s |
| `cline hub start` / `status` / `stop` | running, coreVersion `0.2.0` |
| TUI (opentui render library) | renders the welcome screen |
| peak RSS (TUI) | ~230 MB |

`bun biome check` and `bun -F @cline/cli typecheck` pass. The arm64 musl
binary builds and links against `/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1`, but I have not
run it on aarch64 hardware yet.

Note for the release workflow: musl binaries still need `libstdc++` on the
target system (a 643 KB package on OpenWrt). If you would rather not carry that
dependency, it can be documented or handled in a follow-up — the build itself
does not change.

title: fix(cli): detect npx installs from the Windows npm cache layout
body:
## Summary

`getInstallationInfo` resolves the package manager from the wrapper path, but the npx patterns only match the macOS/Linux npm cache layout (`~/.npm/_npx/...`). On Windows the npx cache lives at `%LocalAppData%\npm-cache\_npx\...`, which does not contain the `/npm/_npx` substring, so `npx cline` falls through to the `/node_modules/` check and is misdetected as a global **npm** install.

Consequences for Windows `npx cline` users:

- `cline update` runs `npm update -g cline --tag latest --min-release-age=0`, creating a global npm installation the user never asked for.

**Issue:** #15284

### Description

With an `openai-compatible` provider, the `/model` picker lists no models when the API key is supplied via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable instead of being stored in `providers.json`. It works when the key is in `providers.json`.

title: fix(llms): explain provider timeouts in plain words and record where they happened
body:
## What was wrong

When a model provider accepts a request and then sends nothing, the run sits for 5 minutes until Bun's built-in fetch timeout gives up. The user then sees only "The operation timed out.", which doesn't say what happened or what to do. Telemetry records the same raw text, so there is no easy way to tell a provider that never started replying from one that stopped partway through.

In the last 7 days, the CLI and Desktop logged about 4,400 of these timeouts, almost all on cheap or free models.

## What this changes

- **Plain message.** When a timeout ends the run, the user sees either "The model provider stopped responding before it started its reply." or "The model provider stopped responding partway through its reply.", followed by "Send a message to continue, or switch models if this keeps happening."
- **Telemetry.** `sdk.error` gets a `timeoutPhase` field (`before_reply` or `mid_reply`), so a model or provider that starts going silent can be spotted and alerted on. The raw error text in telemetry is unchanged.

Retry decisions and time limits are unchanged: a timeout still ends the run after the same wait.

## How it was tested

- New gateway tests make the stream throw Bun's `TimeoutError`, once before any content and once after some text. They check the message the user sees, the raw error text and `timeoutPhase` in `sdk.error`, and that the error is still not retried.
- An end-to-end run through a real hub against a fake provider that goes silent, before replying and partway through, shows the new messages after the usual 300-second wait. Normal replies and dropped connections behave as before.

title: fix(core): stop re-cutting read_files results to the 8k tool-result cap
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Fixes #13923 · [CLINE-3196](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3196)

Related: #13263 (the `read_files` half of it), #14257 (closed in favour of this change).

### Description

A file read passes through two caps that were set independently and never matched up:

- `read_files` bounds its own output at 2000 lines / ~48k characters and tells the model so, both in the tool description and in a per-read footer (`[Showing lines 1-424 of 1500. Use start_line/end_line to read other sections.]`).
- `MessageBuilder` then cuts **every** tool result to 8k characters on the way to the provider, middle-out, with a bare `...[truncated N chars]...` marker.

So a read the model was just told it received in full reaches it ~17% intact. Ranged reads that fit the tool cap carry no footer at all, so there the cut is the only signal — a 345-line range comes back as its first and last ~60 lines. Models respond by paging in ever smaller slices, concluding the tool is broken, and falling back to `cat`/`sed` through the shell (see the issue and the Discord report that prompted this).

The 8k tool-result cap was introduced for command and MCP output, where it was measured; file reads already had a purpose-built cap with paging guidance. `MessageBuilder` also already has a looser 50k cap for file content — user `file` attachments were routed to it precisely so the aggressive tool-result cap would not mutilate them. This change routes read-tool results to that same cap. A well-formed read (≤ ~48.1k with line-number prefixes and footer) is now never re-cut; the 50k cap remains a backstop for a custom read executor that ignores the tool's bounds. Nothing else moves: `run_commands`, search, MCP and custom tools keep the 8k cap; the aggregate 6MB request budget and the stale-read rewrite still bound history growth.

A `maxToolResultChars` that is configured explicitly (option or `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`) keeps its documented meaning of capping every tool result, so it also bounds reads: the read cap is `min(50k, explicit cap)`, and the 50k default only applies when no override is set.

Two existing tests encoded the 8k cut on read fixtures and were adjusted to keep their intent (image siblings preserved while text truncates; stale-read batching counts provider-bound bytes, not raw history bytes) under the read cap.

### Test Procedure

- New unit tests in `message-builder.test.ts` ("read-result cap"): a tool-capped 48k `read_files` window is sent whole (structured and string content), a 60k read result is still cut at the file-content cap, `run_commands` output is still cut at 8k, and an explicit `maxToolResultChars` — as an option and via the env var — still bounds reads while an empty environment keeps the 50k default. The first two fail on `main`.
- New `message-builder.read-files.test.ts` drives the real `read_files` tool through `MessageBuilder` with a 751-line markdown file — whole file, lines 55-400 and lines 110-230, i.e. the reads from the report — plus a batched two-file read, and asserts what the tool returned is what the provider request carries. The single-file cases fail on `main` (7,967 / 7,895 / 7,955 chars of 47,384 / 23,648 / 8,280 reach the model).
- `@cline/core` unit suite, `tsc` and Biome green.

Workaround for affected users until this ships: `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS=50000` in the environment the IDE/CLI starts from (raises the cap for every tool, not only reads).

### Related Issue

**Issue:** https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/15252

### Description

Cline Desktop can import past sessions from Claude Code, Codex and opencode. This adds Cursor.

The new `cursor` adapter in `@cline/core` reads Cursor's local chat store (`User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`). It lists each conversation once, using Cursor's composer id as the source id, so the existing dedup works. Tool calls keep their ids and results, and timestamps, model, workspace folder and git branch carry over. Drafts, subagents, empty conversations and Claude Code mirrors are skipped.

title: feat(checkpoints): explain why a message has no workspace checkpoint
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #XXXX

### Description

Hovering a disabled Reset Code button now explains why the message has no workspace checkpoint, and usually what to do about it. For example: "This git repository has no commits yet, so no checkpoint was taken. Make an initial commit to enable checkpoints." Previously every cause showed the same generic sentence.

Core now records one outcome for each user turn: either a checkpoint, or a `CheckpointFailure` whose `errorMessage` is written for the user. Hosts show that text unchanged, so adding a cause or rewording one needs no proto or webview change. The recorded causes are:

- the workspace isn't a git repository
- the repository has no commits yet (`git init` alone isn't enough, because checkpoints snapshot against `HEAD`)
- git isn't installed
- a snapshot or a custom `createCheckpoint` failed; a callback that throws is recorded, then rethrown as before

Pure bookkeeping lives in `session/checkpoint-records.ts`. `resolveRunCheckpoint(session, runCount)` is the single rule that Reset Code availability, edit-and-regenerate and core restore all use:

- If the turn has a checkpoint, it is used.
- If the turn has a recorded failure, it reports that failure and won't restore files. It no longer falls back to an older checkpoint, which would have quietly undone later turns' work as well.
- Turns with no record, from older sessions or from runs with checkpoints off, fall back to the nearest earlier checkpoint as before. If there is none, the controller asks core to check the current workspace for an explanation.

Restored and edited sessions carry their recorded failures forward alongside their checkpoints. Failures are never pruned, since each one is what stops its run from falling back. A chat-only restore leaves files alone, so a failed snapshot doesn't block it. Desktop edit-forks use the same rule, and `sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the record.

`checkpointExistsForMessage` now returns `{ exists, errorMessage }`. A shared conversion turns that into `{ exists: true } | { exists: false; errorMessage: string | undefined }` on both sides. The webview decides what to show:

- If a checkpoint exists, Reset Code is enabled, whatever the Checkpoints setting.
- If there is no checkpoint and checkpoints are currently disabled, it shows the existing Enable Checkpoints popover with the Settings link.
- Otherwise it shows the backend's explanation, or the old generic sentence if there is none.

Because the setting is read on every render, the explanation updates when the user enables checkpoints, without another lookup.

body:
![Agent team run in the desktop app](https://github.com/cline/cline/raw/saoudrizwan/team-panel-assets-cbd4/team-panel-real-run.gif)

Agent teams worked, but the desktop app gave you almost no way to see that. Teammates' streamed text was interleaved into the lead's transcript. A teammate finishing could mark the lead's turn done. Opening a teammate's session showed nothing until it finished. Nothing told you who was doing what.

This PR gives teams a real UX:

- **Team panel on the chat input.** While a session runs a team, a panel attaches to the top of the input, in the strip the pull request bar uses. Each teammate gets one row:
  - what it is doing now: thinking, reading, editing, running commands, coordinating, waiting, done, or failed;
  - its current step;
  - how long it has been running.
- **Team summary.** The panel header summarizes the team, for example "1 planning · 2 acting · 1 done · 2m 15s". When everyone finishes, the panel folds to that one line and stays as a compact record. It expands again if the team resumes.
- **Opening a teammate.** Selecting a row opens that teammate's session, where the panel stays with that row highlighted. The existing "Main Agent Session" button leads back.
- **Clean lead transcript.** Teammate output no longer renders into the lead's session.
- **Live teammate sessions.** Teammate output is routed into the teammate's own child session, so a teammate you open streams its work live.
- **Shared in `@cline/ui`, with Storybook stories.** `AgentTeamPanel` lives in the UI SDK so other clients can reuse it, along with the helpers that build its rows: `buildAgentTeamMembers` takes a host's teammate-session roster plus `team_progress` lifecycle events. Storybook (`Agent/Team panel`) has a story for every state, including a live replay of a team run.

Making this real meant fixing the places where team data got lost on the hub path:
- `HubRuntimeHost` dropped `team.progress`. It now maps it back to the core `team_progress` event.
- The team progress throttle let streamed chunks overwrite the run activity that says what a teammate is doing. Activity is now sent as it happens; only chunks and heartbeats are throttled.
- The hub projected teammate text, tool, and done events with no agent identity. They are now tagged, and a teammate's `agent.done` is no longer reported as the lead run's done. This matches what in-process sessions already emit.
- The roster only refreshed while the lead looked busy, so runs started while the lead's turn was idle never appeared. It now re-reads on team roster events.

- `tsc` and biome are clean on the changed files.

Real team runs (OpenRouter / Claude Sonnet 4.5) in the native desktop app, after restarting the hub and sidecars:

- the lead transcript stays clean;
- a teammate's session streams live;
- a reviewer run started after the builders finished is picked up;

title: fix(checkpoints): bound concurrent git reads when diffing a checkpoint
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15116

### Description

**Root cause.** `buildCheckpointWorkspaceDiff` (`sdk/packages/core/src/session/checkpoint-diff.ts`) mapped every changed path through a single `Promise.all`, and `readCheckpointFile` spawns one `git show <ref>:<path>` per path (plus a second `git show <ref>^3:<path>` fallback for stash-shaped checkpoints). When the workspace has a large changeset — e.g. untracked build output such as `target/debug/.fingerprint/...` in the issue — this forks one git process per path all at once, which matches the flood of `git show` / `<defunct>` processes in the report.

**Change.** Read paths through a small, order-preserving worker pool (`mapWithConcurrency`, local to the file, no new dependencies) capped at `CHECKPOINT_DIFF_GIT_CONCURRENCY = 8`. Since the two `git show` calls for a path run sequentially, this caps concurrent git children from this function at 8. Output order, content, the equal-content filter, and error propagation are unchanged.

**Non-goals.**
- Does not change which paths are compared. Excluding heavy/ignored directories from checkpoint snapshots is handled separately by #14608.
- Does not batch reads into a single `git cat-file --batch` process; that's a larger refactor and can follow if needed.

title: fix(core): send the reasoning disable to custom models with saved overrides
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Related to #15055 · Linear: [CLINE-3611](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3611/gpt-6-models-bugged-with-azure-openai)

### Description

On OpenAI-compatible endpoints, gpt-5.6/gpt-6 models reject function tools on `/chat/completions` unless the request says `reasoning_effort: "none"`. Users set Reasoning Effort to None, and since #14991 Cline sends `"none"` for any model the catalog doesn't describe. It still went missing for the #15055 reporter after saving None.

**Cause.** A custom model with any saved Model Configuration setting (the Supports Images tick is enough) gets a stored entry with only boolean overlays. `toStoredModelInfo` turns that into a capability list such as `["images", "tools"]`. The gateway's `mayReason` reads a populated list without `"reasoning"` as "this model cannot reason" and skips the disable (`resolvePortableLevel` in `portable-reasoning.ts`). The model then applies its default effort and the endpoint returns the error. The same list shape silently revoked tool calling before #13463, which fixed it by seeding `"tools"`.

**Fix.** Treat a stored entry that says nothing about reasoning as "may reason", the way #13463 treats tools:
- `sdk/packages/core/.../local-provider-registry.ts`: seed `"reasoning"` into a partial overlay list alongside `"tools"`, unless the entry says `supportsReasoning: false`. Catalog-anchored lists stay authoritative, so a genuine no-reasoning catalog model is unchanged.
- `apps/vscode/src/sdk/cline-session-factory.ts`: the same rule in the host's rebuild of legacy boolean snapshots, so the two cannot drift.

**Effects to be aware of.** With None saved, these models now receive `reasoning_effort: "none"`, which is what the catalog-less case already does. A non-reasoning model whose user picked None gets the parameter too; that is a deliberate pick, and the endpoint's error is loud and self-describing, as it is today for unlisted ids. These models may now show a reasoning selector in UIs that gate it on the capability, and the compaction step (which always disables reasoning) sends `"none"` to them, as it already does for unlisted models.

### Test Procedure

- **Fails before, passes after:**
  - `local-provider-service.test.ts` ("seeds tool calling and reasoning …"): a `vision-only` entry gets `images`, `reasoning`, `tools`; a `partial-list` entry gets `reasoning`; `no-reasoning` (`supportsReasoning: false`) keeps it out; the image-generation entry gains neither. Fails on `main` at the partial-list assertion.
  - `cline-session-factory.test.ts`, "keeps an OpenAI Compatible model with saved overrides able to reason": the reporter's path through the real `ProviderSettingsManager` and the real registry (gpt-6-sol on an Azure base URL, `reasoning: { enabled: false }`, a `supportsVision: true` override committed through the store). Fails with the registry change reverted.
  - `cline-session-factory.test.ts`, "treats a dynamic-list model that … accordingly": the host's rebuild seeds reasoning for a legacy boolean snapshot and respects an explicit denial. Fails with the host change reverted.
- **Wire contract:** unchanged. `openai-compatible.wire.test.ts` already pins that a capability list without `reasoning` sends nothing and an unlisted model gets `"none"`; this PR fixes which list these models carry.
- **Updated expectation:** `provider-settings-manager.test.ts` ("registers migrated custom providers …") now expects `reasoning` on a migrated OpenAI Compatible model. That model has no stored entry, so its list is a partial overlay and must not deny reasoning; the exact-list assertion was the only CI failure on the first push.
- **Results:** the full `@cline/core` vitest suite and `bun -F @cline/core typecheck` pass; VS Code `src/sdk` + `src/core/controller` (1467 tests) and `bun run check-types` pass; Biome is clean on the changed files.

title: fix(core): time out unanswered hook capability requests
body:
A remote hook contribution (for example hook.afterRun) was awaited by the hub without a deadline. If the owning client never answered, the pending capability request stayed in the map forever and the session stopped producing output, with no error.

Give capability requests an optional timeout and apply it to hook proxies. On expiry the hub clears the pending entry, publishes capability.resolved (cancelled) so clients stop waiting, and rejects with an error naming the hook and target client. Other capability requests (tool executors, approvals) keep their existing unbounded behavior.

Fixes #13380

title: fix(llms): advance Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoint through tool results
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15167

Also fixes #15307 (same bug, reported independently against the VS Code "Next" engine in v4.1.25).

### Description

With the Anthropic provider, the request carries a single cache breakpoint on the last `user`-role message. Tool results are emitted as `role: "tool"`, and an agent loop adds no new user message between steps, so the breakpoint stays on the original prompt for the whole loop: every assistant/tool turn after it is re-sent as uncached input on every request and never written to the cache.

This PR moves the breakpoint forward: when the newest cacheable message in `buildAiSdkRequestMessages` is a `tool` message, the marker goes on its last `tool-result` part, which `@ai-sdk/anthropic` turns into `cache_control` on the `tool_result` block. It is the Anthropic-path counterpart of the Bedrock fix in #14481. Still exactly one message breakpoint per request, so long loops never approach Anthropic's 4-breakpoint limit.

Scope is limited on purpose:

- Applied only for Claude models on clients that serialize through `@ai-sdk/anthropic`'s converter: the `anthropic` client and `vertex` (which uses it via `@ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic`).
- OpenAI-compatible routes (OpenRouter, gateways, etc.) keep the current placement. Their converter sends tool results as plain-string `tool` messages, so a part marker would end up as a top-level field on the message rather than on a cacheable content block. They likely have the same stuck-breakpoint behavior, but fixing it needs a different wire shape, so I left it for a separate change.

### Test Procedure

- New wire-level test `routing/anthropic-prompt-cache.wire.test.ts` drives the real gateway + `@ai-sdk/anthropic` with a mocked `fetch` and asserts on the JSON body sent to `/v1/messages` (no network). On `main` the two tool-continuation cases fail (the only `cache_control` is on the opening "Fix the bug" text block); with this change all 4 pass: opening prompt, multi-round tool loop, parallel tool results in one step (marker on the last one), and a new human turn after a tool round. Each also checks there is exactly one breakpoint.
- New parametrized gateway test pins the scope: Vertex Claude advances onto the tool result; an OpenRouter Claude route keeps the marker on the last user text and leaves the tool-result part untouched. Verified it fails on `main` for the Vertex case.
- Updated `formats assistant tool calls and tool results into valid AI SDK messages`, which asserted the old placement.
- `@cline/llms`: 1086 passed / 4 skipped, plus the provider VCR playback suite (4/4). `@cline/agents`: 151 passed. `bun run typecheck` for llms and biome format + lint on the changed files are clean.
- `@cline/core test:unit`: 3 failures that also fail on unmodified `main` in my environment (`workspace-manifest` git-remote artifact noted in AGENTS.md, and two `plugin-uninstall` cases that depend on file-permission errors, which don't occur when running as root).

| | share of input read from cache | input cost vs. no caching |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 18.1% | 83.9% |
| this PR | 92.8% | 18.3% |

That's roughly a 4.6× reduction in input cost for that loop.

title: fix(ollama): prevent trailing text-delta after text-end on terminal done chunk
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #XXXX

### Description

Fixes `The run failed: text part <id> not found` errors when streaming responses from the native `ollama` provider (`ollama-ai-provider-v2`).

#### Root Cause

When Ollama finishes streaming from `/api/chat`, its final NDJSON chunk has `done: true` along with `message: { role: "assistant", content: "" }` (or any final delta).

In `ollama-ai-provider-v2@4.0.1`, `OllamaStreamProcessor.processResponseValue` processes `value.done` before `value.message`, and `processTextContent` checks `delta.content != null` (which matches `""`):

1. During the stream (`done: false`), non-empty text chunks emit `text-start` (with `this.state.textId`) followed by `text-delta` parts.
2. On the terminal `done: true` chunk, `handleDoneChunk` runs first and emits `{ type: "text-end", id: this.state.textId }`, causing AI SDK's `streamText` processor to delete `activeTextContent[part.id]`.
3. Immediately afterward on the same chunk, `processDelta` runs for `value.message` and `processTextContent` emits `{ type: "text-delta", id: this.state.textId, delta: "" }`.
4. Because `text-end` was already emitted for `this.state.textId`, AI SDK's `streamText` state machine cannot find the active text part and emits `{ type: "error", error: "text part <id> not found" }`, failing the run.

#### Changes

- **`patches/ollama-ai-provider-v2@4.0.1.patch`**:
  - Process `value.message` (`this.processDelta`) before `value.done` (`this.handleDoneChunk`) in `OllamaStreamProcessor.processResponseValue` so any final delta is emitted before the text/reasoning blocks are closed.
  - Guard `OllamaStreamProcessor.processTextContent` on non-empty `delta.content` (`if (delta == null ? void 0 : delta.content)`)—matching `processThinking`—so empty `content: ""` placeholders on thinking, tool-call, or terminal `done: true` chunks do not open or write to a text part.
- **`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/ollama.ts`**:
  - Document the 5th wire contract covered by the `ollama-ai-provider-v2` patch.
- **`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/ollama.wire.test.ts`**:
  - Add a wire-contract regression test verifying both the raw `LanguageModelV4StreamPart` ordering (`text-start` → `text-delta` → `text-end` with no trailing `text-delta`) and end-to-end execution through AI SDK's `streamText`.

### Test Procedure

- Ran `bun test sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/ollama.wire.test.ts` (all 7 wire-contract tests pass, including the new `streamText` boundary test).
- Verified live against a local Ollama server (`http://localhost:11434`) with `nemotron-3.5-bolt:74b-a9b` (which streams both `message.thinking` and `message.content` followed by a `done: true` chunk with `message.content: ""`), confirming turns complete cleanly with `finishReason: "stop"` and zero stream errors.

## Related Issue
Follow-up to #14767, as noted by @dominiccooney in #14817.

## Description
In `@cline/core` (`hook-file-hooks.ts`), `.ps1` hook files were executed using:

```typescript
[process.platform === "win32" ? "powershell" : "pwsh", "-File", path]
```

title: fix(mcp): re-handshake when a remote server answers with a lost session
body:
Fixes #15147.

NOTE:  This PR was diagnosed and built by cline. I verified the intended result, but lack experience in the code base to validate code quality.   


A remote (streamable HTTP / SSE) MCP server is replaced under a live session — a restart, a
deploy/rollout, a session-TTL sweep. Every tool call after that fails with

```
Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint: Not Found: Session not found
```

and the server never becomes usable again for that session; the user has to restart Cline.

**Root cause.** The session id lives in the server process, so replacing the server orphans it,
while the client's socket stays perfectly healthy. The SDK transport only reconnects SSE *streams*,
and it raises the 404 as an ordinary application error, so nothing in the stack re-initializes:

- `SdkUrlMcpClient.ensureConnectedClient()` returns the cached `Client` — the *session* was dead,
  not the connection.
- `handleOperationError()` marks the error and rethrows. A 404 is not a 401, so no auth handling
  applies either.

The MCP spec puts this recovery on the client ("if the server cannot find the session it MUST
respond 404, and the client SHOULD reinitialize"). The stdio client is unaffected — this is the
remote-client path only.

## Changes — `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/mcp/client.ts`

- **`isMcpSessionLostError()`** classifies by transport status first: `StreamableHTTPError`
  or `SseError` with code 404. An `McpError` is never replayed (the tool may already have run);
  a message naming a missing/expired session is only the fallback for errors that carry no status.
- **`withSessionRecovery()`** wraps `listTools()` and `callTool()`. On a lost session it drops
  the client that produced the 404, opens a fresh session, and replays the operation **once**.
  Every other failure keeps the existing path (`handleOperationError`).
- **`connect()` is single-flight** (`587ab0b`): concurrent callers join one in-flight handshake
  instead of opening one session each. Recovery invalidates by identity, so a straggler cannot
  close the session a sibling just opened, and a call whose signal already aborted is not replayed.
- **`d461778`** snapshots `tools/list` on each successful read and compares it after a
  re-handshake, reporting added / removed / changed tool names once per recovered session through
  `onSessionRecovered`, wired to the session logger by `runtime-builder`. It warns and stops there
  — descriptors are snapshotted at session build and the SDK MCP path has no approval hook, so
  re-registering tools or re-prompting against a changed surface is a separate design.

Recovery is bounded — a second loss reports exactly as before, so a genuinely dead endpoint
cannot put the client in a retry loop.

## Tests — `client-url.test.ts`

- a lost session is recovered with one extra handshake and one close,
- a persistent loss fails after exactly one replay,
- an unrelated error still marks a plain connection error without reconnecting,
- two concurrent callers recover through one shared handshake, and a straggler does not close the
  session a sibling opened,
- a transport 404 that names no session recovers; an `McpError` that mentions one does not,
- an already-aborted call is not replayed,
- a changed surface is reported as added / removed / changed, an unchanged one is not, and a
  failed comparison never fails the recovery.

On the previous head (`e9b85ff`) those five fail: two with `expected 3 to be 2`, the
404-without-message case rejects, and the `McpError` and aborted calls both resolve because they
were replayed.

## Verification

Live A/B, same dead session id, against a real streamable HTTP server, SDK 1.30.0 (as pinned in
`bun.lock`):

```
# unpatched
attempt 1: threw "Streamable HTTP error: ... Not Found: Session not found"  session now deadbeef-...
attempt 2: threw "Streamable HTTP error: ... Not Found: Session not found"  session now deadbeef-...

# patched, identical setup
call with session=deadbeef-... -> OK in 84ms, session now 680347f2-...
unrelated error rethrown: boom (session kept: true)
```

End to end: a CLI/TUI session survived **two** real server rollouts with no restart — the server
log shows the handshake the client performed on its own (`create new session`,
`client_info name: "@cline/core"`) immediately followed by the replayed tool call.

- `bunx vitest run src/extensions/mcp` — 9 files, 95 tests pass
- `bunx vitest run src/runtime/orchestration/runtime-builder.test.ts` — 38 tests pass
- `bun -F @cline/core typecheck` — clean
- `biome check` on the five touched files — clean

Related to #7330, which proposes the same class of recovery for the VS Code extension's own MCP
client (still open); the extension runs its own client outside the hub, so both paths need this.

title: fix(vscode): show the saved reasoning effort and save every pick
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Related to #15055 · Linear: [CLINE-3611](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3611/gpt-6-models-bugged-with-azure-openai)

### Description

The reasoning effort dropdown showed one setting while the session read another:

- **Shown:** the shared per-mode field (`actModeReasoningEffort`). When it's unset, the dropdown falls back to a label the provider passes in: **None** for OpenAI Compatible and most others, **Medium** for Generic, ClinePass, xAI, Z AI and Moonshot.
- **Sent:** the provider's own `providers.json` `reasoning`. It is saved only from the select's `onValueChange`.

Radix's controlled select calls `onValueChange` only when the picked value differs from the one shown (`if (value2 !== prop)` in `@radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state`). So with nothing saved, the dropdown showed "None", picking None again saved nothing, and no `reasoning_effort` was sent. GPT-6 on Azure then applies its default effort and rejects function tools on `/chat/completions`. That's #15055: "None" was selected, yet the error persisted on v4.1.24. In the last 7 days, 107 VS Code users on 4.1.24 hit the same error on OpenAI Compatible.

**Fix:**
- **Host:** `ProviderConfigResponse.reasoning_effort` carries the effort a session started now would request. It's derived from `providers.json` with the session factory's own `normalizeProviderReasoningSettings`, which moves to `sdk/provider-reasoning.ts` so the settings read and the session share one definition without an import cycle.
- **Host:** `WriteProviderConfigPatch.clear_reasoning` removes the saved setting.
- **Host:** any saved setting maps to a level, so "Default" only ever means nothing is saved. A bare `{ enabled: true }`, which the CLI saves for `--thinking`, shows as Medium, the level the gateway requests for it.
- **Webview:** `ReasoningEffortSelector` takes a `value` prop. When it's passed, the dropdown shows that value and adds a **Default** entry for "nothing saved", so every listed level is a real change. Picking Default clears the saved setting, which also gives back the "send nothing" state for endpoints that reject an explicit effort. While the provider config loads, or a reasoning write is still pending, the dropdown is disabled and shows no level: a pick matching a stale display would otherwise count as no change and save nothing.
- **Webview:** `useProviderConfig` exposes no config whose provider id differs from the requested one. `GenericProviderSettings` and `OpenAICompatibleProvider` stay mounted across a provider switch, so the hook used to keep showing the previous provider's state (and let fields be edited against it) until the new read landed. Provider ids are compared case-insensitively, since the host echoes them lowercased.
- **Webview:** the 19 selectors (16 components) that save reasoning per provider take `reasoningEffort` from `useProviderConfig` and save through one shared `reasoningEffortPatch`. Each copied `{ enabled, effort }` patch is removed, along with the `defaultEffort` labels and the default-effort calculations that no longer apply.
- **Unchanged:** OpenAI Native and OpenAI Codex don't save reasoning per provider, so they keep today's behaviour.

**Compatibility:** no stored data is reinterpreted. Nothing saved still sends nothing, so requests are unchanged for existing users; only the label changes from a guessed level to "Default". A cleared setting is the same shape as one that was never set, so both upgrade directions are safe. The new proto fields are additive, so the JetBrains host is unaffected.

### Test Procedure

- **Fails before / passes after:**
  - `ReasoningEffortSelector.test.tsx` drives the real Radix select with user-event. 4 of 6 tests fail against `main`'s selector, including "saves None picked from Default, then clears back to Default" and "is disabled and shows no level while the saved value loads". The other 2 pass by design: one shows that re-picking the shown value reports nothing (the behavior behind the bug), and one covers the unchanged path without `value`.
  - `effective-config.test.ts` and `providerCatalogHandlers.test.ts`: the cases that expose a saved effort, including a bare `{ enabled: true }` as Medium, and the clear request fail with `main`'s `effective-config.ts` and `providerCatalogShared.ts`. The cases that pass on main expect nothing to be exposed.
- **Real store:** `cline-session-factory.test.ts` adds a round trip through the real `ProviderSettingsManager` for an OpenAI Compatible gpt-6 setup. For unset, None, High, Default, then a bare `{ enabled: true }`, it checks that the shown effort matches what the session requests, and that a clear removes `reasoning` from `providers.json`.
- **Hook:** `useProviderConfig.test.ts` adds 5 tests, all failing on `main`'s hook: a switch from provider A to B with B's read unresolved exposes no config and an unknown effort; the host's normalized id still matches; a pending reasoning write reports the effort as unknown, an unrelated write does not, and a failed write clears the pending state.
- **Unit:** `utils/__tests__/reasoningEffort.test.ts` covers the shared patch helper.
- **Wire level (manual, v4.1.24 CLI against a local server that records each request):** saved `{ enabled: false }` sends `reasoning_effort: "none"` for `gpt-6-sol` with tools; nothing saved sends no `reasoning_effort`. That's the core behaviour this UI now drives honestly.
- **Results:**
  - `apps/vscode`: vitest `src/sdk` + `src/core/controller` (1467 tests) pass; `bun run test:unit`, `bun run check-types` and `bun run lint` pass.
  - `webview-ui`: full vitest (628 tests) passes and `tsc -b` is clean.
  - The webview and extension bundles build.
- **Not done:** I didn't click through it in a running VS Code. That's worth a quick manual check: OpenAI Compatible with a fresh provider should show Default, and picking None should then send `reasoning_effort: "none"`.

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Add `delivery: "current_session"` to the agent-facing `tasks` tool so requests such as “check CI tomorrow and report back here” run independently and return their completion or failure to the originating conversation. title: refactor: report terminal model failures at operation boundaries
body:
Model failures could lose their original cause or produce duplicate terminal reports. Give the outermost operation ownership of terminal reporting and preserve structured failure details through the provider, gateway, and agent boundaries.

## Fixes

- Replace flattened finish error fields and `errorReported` coordination with `failure: AgentModelFailure`, carrying the display message, stable diagnostic message, original cause, classification, turn-level retry decision, and correlation context. Update all producers, consumers, and tests.
- Report one terminal failure at the operation boundary: agent runs report after recovery is exhausted; standalone gateway streams report at their terminal boundary. Providers maintain tracing spans without separately emitting terminal `sdk.error` events.
- Preserve native TimeoutError attribution after a completed internal model-tool step. The AI SDK serializes the public abort reason to a string, so consult the captured structured timeout and original signal reason instead of producing a generic unknown-finish error.
- Preserve provider failure details through all terminal context-overflow paths: recovery disabled, nothing to compact, and overflow persisting after compaction. The overflow wrapper carries the structured failure and original cause, retaining status/code, error phase, AI SDK call ID, and request ID on the single terminal `sdk.error`, plus the original provider error in `result.error.cause`. The actionable overflow message remains intact.
- Keep request IDs in display messages and correlation metadata while using stable diagnostic messages for telemetry deduplication. Use camelCase for caller-supplied context fields, including `errorPhase` and `errorTurnRetryable`.

## `isRetryable` and retry behavior

Keep the unmodified AI SDK 7.0.120 retry implementation. This PR does **not** add an `isRetryable` gate, stream backoff, or provider-tool replay guard, and does not upgrade the SDK. The dependency remains `^7.0.120`; the lockfile resolves 7.0.120.

- Request-start failures use `maxRetries: 5`, with the SDK's recognized-error retryability checks and retry-after-aware exponential backoff.
- Provider error parts received after streaming starts use `streamRetries: 3`. In this SDK version, automatic stream retries **do not check `isRetryable` and have no explicit backoff**. An error marked `isRetryable: false` can therefore still trigger automatic stream recovery.
- Preserve the original structured error, including its retryability metadata, in `failure.cause`. `failure.retryable` and `errorTurnRetryable` describe eligibility for an additional **whole-turn** retry; they are distinct from the provider error's `isRetryable`. Terminal stream errors and exhausted request-start RetryErrors do not receive another whole-turn retry budget.

## Validation

SDK build; llms, agents, and core typechecks; lint; 1,079 llms tests, 158 agent tests, and 14 core adapter tests passed. Coverage includes a real gateway/Cline-provider/AI-SDK/AgentRuntime timeout after a completed web search, original error and correlation retention, one terminal report per operation, all three unrecoverable context-overflow paths (including the latest failure after compaction), recovered runs, and failed-attempt span export.

Agent terminal reports use `component=agents`, `operation=agent.run`; standalone gateway reports use the llms operation boundary.
